```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# paths in this document are relative to the repository root, whether knitting
# or running chunks interactively
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_rstudio_project))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)
```

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(yaml)
library(knitr)
```

This standalone analysis (not part of the {targets} pipeline) informs whether
lakeSR should mask Landsat 8/9 pixels with medium **and** high `SR_QA_AEROSOL`
levels (the documented rule) or mask only high levels and flag medium. See
AquaSat/AquaMatch_siteSR#47 for background.

For each sampled lake and Landsat 8/9 scene, high-confidence water pixels
(DSWE 1) were selected using the production masks (clouds, hillshadow,
realistic values, sun glint), **without** the aerosol mask. Water pixels were
then tallied by aerosol level (bits 6-7), and median reflectance was calculated
for each aerosol level and under each candidate masking rule:

- **nomask**: no aerosol mask (climatology, low, medium, high retained)
- **nohigh**: mask high (climatology, low, medium retained)
- **nomedhigh**: mask medium and high (climatology, low retained; the documented rule)

```{r load}
cfg <- read_yaml("aerosol_spot_check/config_aero_check.yml")
min_pix <- cfg$gee_settings$min_no_pix
smoke_years <- unlist(cfg$temporal_settings$smoke_years)

sample_prs <- read_csv("aerosol_spot_check/out/sample_pathrows.csv",
                       col_types = cols(WRS2_PR = "c"))

files <- list.files(params$down_dir, pattern = "^lakeSR_aero_check_LS89_.*\\.csv$",
                    full.names = TRUE)
if (length(files) == 0) stop("No exports found in ", params$down_dir,
                             ". Run 03_download_results.R first.")

levels_aero <- c("clim", "low", "med", "high")
bands <- c("Aerosol", "Blue", "Green", "Red", "Nir")

dat <- map(files, \(fp) read_csv(fp, col_types = cols(id = "c", WRS2_PR = "c",
                                                       .default = "?"))) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("pCount_"), \(x) replace_na(x, 0)),
         date = as.Date(DATE_ACQUIRED),
         year = year(date),
         season = case_when(month(date) %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "DJF",
                            month(date) %in% 3:5 ~ "MAM",
                            month(date) %in% 6:8 ~ "JJA",
                            TRUE ~ "SON") %>%
           factor(levels = c("DJF", "MAM", "JJA", "SON")),
         smoke = if_else(year %in% smoke_years, "smoke year", "non-smoke year"),
         satellite = str_replace(SPACECRAFT_ID, "LANDSAT_", "LS")) %>%
  left_join(sample_prs %>% select(WRS2_PR, ecoregion), by = "WRS2_PR")
```

## Coverage

`r nrow(dat)` site-scenes with at least one DSWE 1 water pixel, from
`r n_distinct(dat$id)` lakes, `r n_distinct(dat$LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID)` scenes and
`r n_distinct(dat$WRS2_PR)` of `r nrow(sample_prs)` path-rows
(`r min(dat$date)` to `r max(dat$date)`).

```{r coverage}
dat %>%
  group_by(ecoregion) %>%
  summarize(path_rows = n_distinct(WRS2_PR),
            lakes = n_distinct(id),
            scenes = n_distinct(LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID),
            site_scenes = n(),
            water_pixels = sum(pCount_water)) %>%
  arrange(desc(water_pixels)) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Share of water pixels by aerosol level

Shares are pixel-weighted (each DSWE 1 water pixel counts once).

```{r level-share}
level_long <- dat %>%
  select(id, LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID, ecoregion, season, smoke, satellite, year,
         all_of(paste0("pCount_", levels_aero))) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("pCount_"), names_to = "level", values_to = "pixels",
               names_prefix = "pCount_") %>%
  mutate(level = factor(level, levels = levels_aero,
                        labels = c("climatology", "low", "medium", "high")))

share_by <- function(df, ...) {
  df %>%
    group_by(..., level) %>%
    summarize(pixels = sum(pixels), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
    mutate(share = pixels / sum(pixels)) %>%
    ungroup()
}

overall <- share_by(level_long)
overall %>%
  mutate(share = scales::percent(share, 0.1)) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

plot_share <- function(df, x, title) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = {{ x }}, y = share, fill = level)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "magma", begin = 0.15, end = 0.85, direction = -1) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "share of water pixels", fill = "aerosol level", title = title) +
    theme_bw()
}
```

```{r share-ecoregion, fig.height = 6}
share_by(level_long, ecoregion) %>%
  plot_share(ecoregion, "By ecoregion") +
  coord_flip()
```

```{r share-season-smoke, fig.height = 7}
share_by(level_long, ecoregion, season) %>%
  plot_share(season, "By season and ecoregion") +
  facet_wrap(~ ecoregion, ncol = 5)

share_by(level_long, ecoregion, smoke) %>%
  plot_share(smoke, "Smoke vs. non-smoke years, by ecoregion") +
  facet_wrap(~ ecoregion, ncol = 5) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r share-year-sat}
share_by(level_long, year) %>%
  plot_share(factor(year), "By year")

share_by(level_long, satellite) %>%
  plot_share(satellite, "By satellite")
```

## Interpolated aerosol and valid retrievals over water

If most water pixels carry the interpolated flag (bit 5), the aerosol level
over lakes largely reflects retrievals from surrounding land.

```{r interp}
dat %>%
  group_by(ecoregion) %>%
  summarize(water_pixels = sum(pCount_water),
            pct_interpolated = 100 * sum(pCount_interp) / water_pixels,
            pct_valid_retrieval = 100 * sum(pCount_valid) / water_pixels) %>%
  bind_rows(dat %>%
              summarize(ecoregion = "All",
                        water_pixels = sum(pCount_water),
                        pct_interpolated = 100 * sum(pCount_interp) / water_pixels,
                        pct_valid_retrieval = 100 * sum(pCount_valid) / water_pixels)) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("pct"), \(x) round(x, 1))) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Site-scenes retained under each rule

A site-scene is retained if at least `r min_pix` water pixels remain after
aerosol masking (the production minimum). **as_coded** is the inverted mask
used to create the released Landsat 8/9 data (medium and high retained).

```{r retention}
retained <- dat %>%
  transmute(id, LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID, ecoregion, smoke,
            nomask = pCount_water,
            nohigh = pCount_clim + pCount_low + pCount_med,
            nomedhigh = pCount_clim + pCount_low,
            as_coded = pCount_med + pCount_high) %>%
  pivot_longer(nomask:as_coded, names_to = "rule", values_to = "pixels") %>%
  mutate(rule = factor(rule, levels = c("nomask", "nohigh", "nomedhigh", "as_coded")),
         kept = pixels >= min_pix)

retained %>%
  group_by(rule) %>%
  summarize(site_scenes_kept = sum(kept),
            pct_of_nomask = NA_real_) %>%
  mutate(pct_of_nomask = round(100 * site_scenes_kept / site_scenes_kept[rule == "nomask"], 1)) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

retained %>%
  group_by(ecoregion, rule) %>%
  summarize(kept = sum(kept), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  mutate(pct_of_nomask = kept / kept[rule == "nomask"]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(rule != "nomask") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ecoregion, y = pct_of_nomask, fill = rule)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "site-scenes retained, relative to no aerosol mask",
       title = paste0("Site-scenes with at least ", min_pix, " water pixels")) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Low vs. medium aerosol mix within site-scenes

Each site-scene's summary is a median of its water pixels, so the mix of low
and medium pixels in a site-scene determines how much medium pixels can affect
that median. This section looks at site-scenes retained when only high
aerosol is masked (at least `r min_pix` climatology, low, or medium pixels).
If most site-scenes are entirely low or entirely medium, the share of low
pixels is a good proxy for which pixels make up the median.

```{r low-med-mix}
mix <- dat %>%
  mutate(n_lowmed = pCount_clim + pCount_low + pCount_med,
         p_low = (pCount_clim + pCount_low) / n_lowmed) %>%
  filter(n_lowmed >= min_pix) %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(p_low, c(-Inf, 0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1 - 1e-9, Inf),
                   labels = c("0%\n(all medium)", "0–10%", "10–25%", "25–50%",
                              "50–75%", "75–90%", "90–100%", "100%\n(all low)")))

mix_bins <- mix %>%
  count(bin, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n))

ggplot(mix_bins, aes(x = bin, y = pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3b6ea8", width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(pct, 0.1)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.2,
            color = "grey20") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = "share of low aerosol pixels among low + medium water pixels",
       y = "share of site-scenes",
       title = "Most site-scenes are entirely low or entirely medium aerosol",
       subtitle = paste0(format(nrow(mix), big.mark = ","),
                         " site-scenes retained when masking high aerosol only")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

`r scales::percent(mean(mix$p_low %in% c(0, 1)), 0.1)` of these site-scenes
are entirely low or entirely medium, and
`r scales::percent(mean(mix$p_low <= 0.1 | mix$p_low >= 0.9), 0.1)` have at
most 10% or at least 90% low pixels.

The table below compares the number of site-scenes kept by masking medium and
high (the documented rule) with masking high only and letting users filter on
the share of low pixels. Percentages are relative to site-scenes with at least
`r min_pix` water pixels and no aerosol mask.

```{r low-share-filter}
n_nomask <- sum(dat$pCount_water >= min_pix)

tibble(approach = c("mask high only",
                    "mask high only, then filter to ≥ 50% low",
                    "mask high only, then filter to ≥ 75% low",
                    "mask high only, then filter to ≥ 90% low",
                    "mask high only, then filter to 100% low",
                    "mask medium and high (documented rule)"),
       site_scenes = c(nrow(mix),
                       sum(mix$p_low >= 0.5),
                       sum(mix$p_low >= 0.75),
                       sum(mix$p_low >= 0.9),
                       sum(mix$p_low == 1),
                       sum(dat$pCount_clim + dat$pCount_low >= min_pix))) %>%
  mutate(pct_of_nomask = round(100 * site_scenes / n_nomask, 1)) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Reflectance by aerosol level

### Within site-scene

Where a single site-scene has at least `r min_pix` pixels at a given aerosol
level **and** at least `r min_pix` climatology/low pixels, the median
reflectance at that level is compared to the climatology/low median from the
same scene and lake. Mixed-level site-scenes may be uncommon because aerosol
level varies smoothly in space.

```{r within-scene}
refl_long <- dat %>%
  select(id, LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID, ecoregion, smoke, season,
         pCount_clim, pCount_low, pCount_med, pCount_high,
         matches(paste0("^med_(", paste(bands, collapse = "|"), ")_"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("med_"), names_to = c("band", "group"),
               names_pattern = "med_(.*)_(.*)", values_to = "refl")

ref_lowclim <- refl_long %>%
  filter(group == "nomedhigh", pCount_clim + pCount_low >= min_pix) %>%
  select(id, LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID, band, ref = refl)

within <- refl_long %>%
  filter((group == "med" & pCount_med >= min_pix) |
           (group == "high" & pCount_high >= min_pix)) %>%
  inner_join(ref_lowclim, by = c("id", "LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID", "band")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(refl), !is.na(ref)) %>%
  mutate(diff = refl - ref,
         pct_diff = 100 * diff / ref,
         band = factor(band, levels = bands),
         group = factor(group, levels = c("med", "high"),
                        labels = c("medium", "high")))

within %>%
  group_by(group, band) %>%
  summarize(n_site_scenes = n(),
            median_diff = median(diff),
            median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff),
            q25_pct_diff = quantile(pct_diff, 0.25),
            q75_pct_diff = quantile(pct_diff, 0.75),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3))) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r within-scene-plot}
# axis limits that show every box and whisker in full (plus zero); outliers
# beyond the whiskers can fall outside, and are counted in the caption
whisker_limits <- function(df, ...) {
  ext <- df %>%
    group_by(...) %>%
    summarize(lo = boxplot.stats(diff)$stats[1],
              hi = boxplot.stats(diff)$stats[5],
              .groups = "drop")
  lims <- range(c(ext$lo, ext$hi, 0))
  lims + c(-1, 1) * 0.05 * diff(lims)
}

outlier_caption <- function(df, lims) {
  n_out <- sum(df$diff < lims[1] | df$diff > lims[2])
  paste0(n_out, " of ", format(nrow(df), big.mark = ","),
         " values (all outliers beyond the whiskers) lie outside the plotted range")
}

if (nrow(within) > 0) {
  lims <- whisker_limits(within, group, band)
  ggplot(within, aes(x = band, y = diff, fill = group)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = lims) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "median reflectance minus climatology/low median (same scene)",
         fill = "aerosol level", caption = outlier_caption(within, lims)) +
    theme_bw()
}
```

### Within lake, across scenes

Each site-scene is assigned its dominant aerosol level (the level with the
most water pixels). For each lake, the median reflectance across scenes
dominated by medium or high aerosol is compared to the lake's median across
scenes dominated by climatology/low aerosol. Seasonal and smoke-year
differences in water quality can contribute to these differences, so they
complement the within-scene comparison rather than replace it.

```{r within-lake}
dominant <- dat %>%
  filter(pCount_water >= min_pix) %>%
  mutate(dominant = case_when(
    pCount_clim + pCount_low >= pmax(pCount_med, pCount_high) ~ "clim/low",
    pCount_med >= pCount_high ~ "medium",
    TRUE ~ "high")) %>%
  select(id, LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID, ecoregion, dominant,
         all_of(paste0("med_", bands, "_nomask"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("med_"), names_to = "band", values_to = "refl",
               names_pattern = "med_(.*)_nomask")

within_lake <- dominant %>%
  group_by(id, ecoregion, band, dominant) %>%
  summarize(refl = median(refl, na.rm = TRUE), n_scenes = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(id, ecoregion, band), names_from = dominant,
              values_from = refl) %>%
  pivot_longer(any_of(c("medium", "high")), names_to = "group", values_to = "refl") %>%
  filter(!is.na(refl), !is.na(`clim/low`)) %>%
  mutate(diff = refl - `clim/low`,
         pct_diff = 100 * diff / `clim/low`,
         band = factor(band, levels = bands),
         group = factor(group, levels = c("medium", "high")))

within_lake %>%
  group_by(group, band) %>%
  summarize(n_lakes = n(),
            median_diff = median(diff),
            median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff),
            q25_pct_diff = quantile(pct_diff, 0.25),
            q75_pct_diff = quantile(pct_diff, 0.75),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3))) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r within-lake-ecoregion, fig.height = 6}
if (nrow(within_lake) > 0) {
  within_lake_blue <- within_lake %>% filter(band == "Blue")
  lims <- whisker_limits(within_lake_blue, group, ecoregion)
  ggplot(within_lake_blue, aes(x = ecoregion, y = diff, fill = group)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4) +
    coord_flip(ylim = lims) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "lake median Blue minus clim/low-dominated median",
         fill = "dominant level", caption = outlier_caption(within_lake_blue, lims)) +
    theme_bw()
}
```

## Effect of the masking rule on reported reflectance

For site-scenes retained under both rules, the difference between the
site-scene median reflectance reported under **nomask** or **nohigh** and
under **nomedhigh** (the documented rule). This shows how much the choice of
rule would change the values in lakeSR, separately from how many observations
it removes.

```{r rule-effect}
rule_pix <- retained %>%
  select(id, LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID, rule, pixels) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = pixels, names_prefix = "pix_")

rule_effect <- refl_long %>%
  filter(group %in% c("nomask", "nohigh", "nomedhigh")) %>%
  select(id, LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID, ecoregion, band, group, refl) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = refl) %>%
  left_join(rule_pix, by = c("id", "LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID")) %>%
  filter(pix_nomedhigh >= min_pix) %>%
  transmute(id, LANDSAT_PRODUCT_ID, ecoregion,
            band = factor(band, levels = bands),
            nomask = nomask - nomedhigh,
            nohigh = nohigh - nomedhigh) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(nomask, nohigh), names_to = "rule", values_to = "diff")

rule_effect %>%
  group_by(rule, band) %>%
  summarize(n_site_scenes = n(),
            n_changed = sum(abs(diff) > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_diff = median(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_abs_diff = mean(abs(diff), na.rm = TRUE),
            p95_abs_diff = quantile(abs(diff), 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3))) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Takeaways

_Written from the 2026-10-19 run (25 path-rows, 2019–2023). Some numbers below
(ecoregion, season and dominant-level breakdowns) were calculated from the same
exports but are not printed as tables above. Update this section if the sample
or the pull changes._

**Masking high aerosol is clearly justified. Masking medium as well (the
documented rule) is defensible, but costs a substantial share of observations.**

1. **Medium and high aerosol cover about 43% of DSWE 1 water pixels, not the
   ~85% reported in siteSR#47.** Overall, 57% of water pixels are low, 26%
   medium and 17% high; none are climatology. The share varies by region, from
   30% medium/high in Mediterranean California to 71% in the Marine West Coast
   Forest (coastal southeast Alaska). It also varies by season: about 48% in
   spring and summer and 36% in fall and winter. Smoke years differ only
   slightly from other years (44% vs. 41%), and Landsat 8 and 9 are similar.
   The 85% figure likely reflects where the reporter's siteSR matchups are.

2. **The aerosol level over lakes is almost entirely interpolated from land.**
   About 89% of water pixels carry the interpolated-aerosol flag (bit 5) in
   every ecoregion, and only 1.6% have a valid aerosol retrieval. The aerosol
   QA level for a lake therefore mostly reflects conditions over the
   surrounding land.

3. **Medium-aerosol pixels are consistently darker than low-aerosol pixels in
   the same lake and scene.** In 1,124 site-scenes with at least 8 pixels at
   both levels, the median Blue reflectance of medium pixels is lower by about
   0.004. That is roughly 20% of typical Blue water reflectance (about 0.018).
   The difference is negative in 93–100% of site-scenes in every ecoregion, and
   Green, Red and Nir are also lower (by about 7–10%). This is consistent with
   over-correction of path radiance over dark water when the atmospheric
   correction assumes a higher aerosol load. Pixels with different levels may
   sit in different parts of a lake, so location is not fully ruled out, but
   the consistency across regions suggests a real bias.

4. **Scenes dominated by high aerosol appear contaminated.** Compared with
   scenes dominated by low aerosol, they are brighter (median Blue 0.024 vs.
   0.018, Nir 0.027 vs. 0.016) and cloudier (median scene cloud cover 21% vs.
   7%). This is consistent with residual haze or thin cloud and supports the
   USGS guidance against using high-aerosol pixels. Only 17 site-scenes had
   enough high and low pixels for a same-scene comparison, so this relies on
   the comparison across scenes.

5. **The choice of rule mainly decides which observations exist, not their
   values.** Relative to no aerosol mask, masking high only keeps 84% of
   site-scenes with at least 8 water pixels, and masking medium and high keeps
   60%. The inverted mask used for the released Landsat 8/9 data keeps only
   44%, and those are exactly the medium/high-aerosol pixels shown above to be
   darker (medium) or contaminated (high). Most site-scenes (69%) have a
   single aerosol level, so for site-scenes retained under both rules, adding
   medium pixels barely changes the median (95th percentile difference: 0.002
   in Blue).

6. **Most site-scenes are entirely low or entirely medium aerosol.** Among
   site-scenes retained when only high aerosol is masked, 74% contain only one
   of the two levels (54% all low, 21% all medium), and 83% are at least 90%
   one level. Most of the extra site-scenes gained by keeping medium pixels
   are therefore made up entirely of medium-aerosol pixels.

**Decision:** we are fixing the inverted mask and keeping the documented rule
of masking medium **and** high aerosol pixels, accepting the apparent "loss" of
site-scenes relative to masking high only (60% vs. 84%) in order to retain
high-quality data. That loss is only apparent. The alternative of masking high
only and passing the choice to users through a percent-low-aerosol flag would
leave quality-minded users with *fewer* observations: filtering to at least
50% low pixels keeps 59% of site-scenes, at least 90% keeps 50%, and 100%
keeps 45%. Masking medium and high retains 60%, more than any of those
filters, because each site-scene's median is calculated from its low-aerosol
pixels alone rather than discarding any site-scene that contains medium
pixels. It also avoids the consistent dark bias of medium-aerosol pixels
(point 3) and matches the documentation that passed USGS review.

**Caveats:** this is a sample of 25 path-rows over 2019–2023. The same-scene
comparison is limited to mixed-level site-scenes, which may be transition
zones. The size of the medium-aerosol bias has not yet been compared with the
between-mission differences that the intermission handoffs correct for.
